transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. AI. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. AI. Well, the main reason I’m here is that I'm having a lot of trouble at work. I'm a nurse, and when I'm on the floor, I just lose my train of thought constantly. Like, an IV pump will beep, or I'll hear someone ask another nurse a question, or a call light goes off... and suddenly I’ve completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was just working on. It happens all the time, and it's really starting to affect my job.
Did you have similar problems with attention or distractibility as a child?

Yes, I did. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright, but really careless. I was just always losing my worksheets or completely forgetting to actually turn in my homework once I did it. It was a constant issue, so my mom actually had to sit down with me every single night while I did my work just to keep me on track and make sure I finished things.
Do you also tend to feel very restless or fidgety, as if you have to move around a lot?

No, not really. I don't feel like I have to be moving around all the time, and I wouldn't say I'm restless or fidgety. It's more just... my brain losing track of things, rather than my body needing to move.
Do these attention problems also happen in settings outside of work, like at home or in other parts of your life?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't noticed it as much at home. Um... I guess because work is so fast-paced and high-stakes, that's where it really stands out to me. But at home or in other parts of my life... I don't know, I just don't really have any specific examples of it happening. I've mostly just been focused on how bad it's getting at the hospital.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things most days?

No, I wouldn't say I worry a lot. I mean, I stress about making mistakes at work because of the attention stuff, but I don't have, like, a general problem with worrying about different things all the time. It's really just the focus issues that are bothering me.
Do these focus and distractibility problems happen in more than one setting, like at home as well as at work?

I think we actually just touched on that. Like I said, I haven't really noticed it much outside of the hospital. Work is just so demanding that my mistakes are really obvious there. At home... I really don't have any examples of it being an issue. It's just work where I'm really struggling with it.
Did these attention problems start before you were 12 years old?

Yeah, they actually did. Even back in elementary school, it was an issue. My teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright but really careless. I was always losing my worksheets or completely forgetting to turn in my homework. My mom actually had to sit down with me every single night just to keep me on track and make sure I got things done.
Do you often act on impulse, such as interrupting others or blurt out answers before a question is finished?

No, not really. I'm usually pretty quiet, actually. I don't really interrupt people or blurt things out. I'm more likely to just space out while someone is talking rather than jump in and cut them off.
Do these attention problems cause you trouble in more than one part of your life, not just at work?

I think we actually just went over this a minute ago. Like I said, it really is just at work. I haven't noticed it causing trouble in other parts of my life, like at home. It's pretty much just at the hospital where I'm really having a hard time with it.
Do you feel anxious or worried for much of the day, most days?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I get stressed sometimes, especially with how things are going at work right now, but I wouldn't say I'm anxious or worried most of the day. It's really just the focus and getting my tasks done that's the main issue.
